The great Prasa halt

By: Anina Peens | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
railway transport grinding to a halt...

Unique Selling Point:
Is the provision of security by MK members on Prasa railways the
solution to the protection of the railways?

Summary:
South Africans are not using trains anymore. The railways are destroyed. Trains on the main line in Cape Town have to stop 12km outside the city because illegal land invaders have occupied the railways and they are not going to move soon. MK veterans will now be given the power to protect, and community members will be paid to do what?


Further information:
Shortly after the minister of transport, Fikile Mbalula appointed Zolani Matthews as the new CEO of PRASA, who critics say is too old and does not have the skills or experience to restore the embattled state-owned enterprise, the minister had another surprise up his sleeve.
MK members will now be deployed to secure the railways.
These MK members will be working with local communities living around the railway lines, who will be paid a stipend to help protect the railways.
This is Mbalula’s plan to blow life back into the perished railway system. He has also suggested to the new CEO, Zolani Matthews that his immediate focus should be to curb corruption within PRASA and get rid of those who are just there to “eat”. This, while train services that are supposed to cater for the poorest of the poor, are practically non-existent. And as a result, they have learned not to depend on railway transport.

The National Household transport survey was just released by STATSSA and shows a 45% decrease since 2013, in the number of people dependent on the railway system.

THE GREAT PRASA HALT

STRAP: CARTE BLANCHE JULY 2020

VO
It was mid-2020…Level-5 lockdown. Passenger travel had been suspended, and Carte Blanche revealed how vandals were destroying the country’s railway lines.

The Passenger Railway Agency of South Africa or PRASA told us that 3000 security guards would be deployed by August 2020.

Fast forward nine months and the situation has taken a turn for the worse.

Without any workable security plan realized, vandalized infrastructure is but one of many challenges now dragging the state-owned enterprise to its knees.

Opening of new story

On the central line outside Cape Town, 7000 shacks have been erected on the train tracks. If one shack houses four people – it could mean that nearly 30 thousand people have illegally invaded PRASA’s tracks.

DEREK LINK
FILE ON HARDDRIVE: 17 MARCH PRASA: PRIVATE: XDROOT
CLIP 0196
“You’ve heard of living close to the edge? Well, some of these shacks are putting their lives right on the line, well that is if the trains were running”

VO
Cape Town’s central line in is a key service for commuters from all over the Western Cape. While it will cost billions to repair the railway, the service cannot be reinstated if illegal land invaders are not moved.

FILE ON HARDDRIVE: 17 MARCH PRASA: PRIVATE: XDROOT
CLIP 0175
10’34’00’15”
SUPER@MLONDOLOZI MAGQAZI, ILLEGAL LAND INVADOR
“PRASA must fix the cables then the trains so the trains can operate. Why the trains are not operating is not because of the shacks”

VO
Mlondolozi Magqazi is a community leader of the Siyahlala informal settlement who believes it’s PRASA’s fault that the land invaders are not getting basic services like rubbish removal or sanitation.

FILE ON HARDDRIVE: 17 MARCH PRASA: PRIVATE: XDROOT
CLIP 0175
10’39’01’10”
SUPER@MLONDOLOZI MAGQAZI, COMMUNITY LEADER, SIYAHLAHLA
“We know we are getting in there within there without permission, but we are there now and we have rights. And from now on I blame PRASA, because it is the PRASA now have to make a plan about us.”
MOVE THIS BYTE HERE BACK TO BACK

DEREK LINK
FILE ON HARDDRIVE: 17 MARCH PRASA: PRIVATE: XDROOT
CLIP 0148
“The last trains ran on these lines in March last year, the beginning of the lockdown. And since then, the settlement has grown and a lot of the infrastructure has disappeared, like the overhead lines”

VO
Transport minister Fikile Mbalula maintains the land was invaded during hard lockdown, when no trains were running, and the shack dwellers are now the state’s problem.

FILE ON HARRDRIVE: JACO PRASA: MINISTER
8’01’55’43’-8’02’51’00’
SUPER@ FIKILE MBALULA, MINISTER OF TRANSPORT
“It’s a mess, it is a mess, and it shouldn’t have been allowed. The first person that put up a shack there was supposed to be dealt with accordingly and told to move… they have settled there, and the numbers have grown exponentially because they know government has got an obligation to find them land you can’t just remove them.”

FILE ON HARDDRIVE: 17 MARCH PRASA: PRIVATE: XDROOT
CLIP 0213
11’10’00’15’
DEREK
“The minister and PRASA say that this community only started living here after lockdown, after March last year?”
SUPER@THEMBELA RADEBE, SQUATTER
“That’s not true. It is for a long time, many years we are staying here, lockdown was only last year. It is many years we stay here. You can see this cement here; it is not from last year.”

VO
Thembela Radebe says he moved to Siyahlala with his extended family before lockdown.

FILE FROM HARDDRIVE: 17 MARCH PRASA
CLIP 0213
11’01’26’24
SUPER@THEMBELA RADEBE, SQUATTER
I buy the temporary hoki, because I see the empty space next to the Prasa space.”
FILE FROM HARDDRIVE: 17 MARCH PRASA
CLIP 0213
11’01’26’24
DEREK
“But Thembela, if it is PRASA land, isn’t it fair enough if they say you have to move? It is their property?”
SUPER@THEMBELA RADEBE, SQUATTER
“Prasa is a national railway lines, which means it is our government. So, to get to place to stay is not like we are asking them for that, they have to do it. Out government have to do it.”

VO
Appointed chair of the board last October to turn around the embattled utility, Leonard Ramathlakane says PRASA is working with the City of Cape Town to find alternative land for the community.

FILE FROM HARD DRIVE: CARTE BLANCHE: JACO: CHAIRPERSON
CLIP 01980003
8’16’07’35’-18’16’32’01
SUPER@ LEONARD RAMATLAKANE: PRASA CHAIRMAN
“I personally delivered notices of, I don’t want to call it eviction, I delivered notices that they should leave that place because they are illegally squatting on the rail reserve, some on top of the line.

VO
Minister Mbalula is convinced the community will be gone by June.

FILE FROM HARDDRIVE: CARTE BLANCHE: JACO
SUPER@ FIKILE MBALULA, MINISTER OF TRANSPORT
8’03’47’28’
the sooner we rebuild the corridors at least we will be operational. Once we removed the people who have built shacks on the rail line, half of the job will be done…

FILE ON HARDDRIVE: 17 MARCH PRASA
CLIP 0205/ CLIP 0207 (ANY OF THESE TWO LINKS CAN WORK)
“Well, the minister may feel that the community is going to leave but as far as we can see, they are staying, they are even building. And that is what Siyahahla means, what does it mean? WE ARE STAYING (Someone else says that)

VO
The United National Transport Union or UNTU, the majority labour union in PRASA, blames Mbalula for PRASA’s lost infrastructure, because he’d suspended the services of 20 security companies in 2019.

A007C164_21031554
12’28”-13’00”
SUPER@ STEVE HARRIS: UNTU PRESIDENT
“What the minister should have done he should have either continued with those security contracts knowing full well that he will sit with open lines. I mean, our lines are open, you
VO
UNTU says it made several suggestions to Mbalula in the past, which appeared to be ignored.

SUPER@ STEVE HARRIS: UNTU PRESIDENT
13’15”- 13’33”
“Had the minister engaged with us or listened to us in 2019 when we requested that the South African defense force be brought in to protect the assets only, we would not have sat with the vandalization that we are facing today.”

VO
Mbalula says PRASA only has itself to blame.

SUPER@ FIKILE MBALULA; TRANSPORT MINISTER
7’52’24’47’-7’52’41’19’
“No, it was not my decision…the mistake of the board was to suspend them without any contingency plan meaning… but these security companies, if you want my view, they were not helping.

VO
Amid the prolonged security challenge, PRASA believes it will be profitable again. But commuter numbers have plummeted. We visited two stations that are still operational in the Western Cape.

FILE ON HARDDRIVE: DEREK TAKES A TRAIN RIDE
CLIP 1799
“We are at Pinelands station, the security guard says the trains are running, but there is no one at the ticket office. So, we will try and wait for the next train”

VO
We waited for the train for over an hour and met Tina Williams, the only other commuter on the platform. She still often commutes between home and work.

FILE ON HARDDRIVE: DEREK TAKES TRAIN RIDE
DEREK INTERVIEW WITH TINA
01’06
SUPER@ TINA WILLIAMS, COMMUTER
Die oggend treine het n sekere tyd maar die na agt uur het nie ‘n tyd wat hulle kom nie.
PLEASE ADD SUBTITLES
“In the mornings the trains come at certain times, but after eight o’ clock, there is no timetable”
DEREK
“And in the mornings, you buy a ticket...”
SUPER@ TINA WILLIAMS, COMMUTER
“Ja en in die middag buy ek nie ‘n ticket nie, ek travel free”
PLEASE ADD SUBTITLES
“Yes in the afternoon I don’t buy a ticket, I travel for free”

VO
When the train finally arrived, Williams had been waiting for over three hours. Although there were security personnel on coaches, no one checked tickets and by the afternoon rush-hour, the ticket office was shut.

FILE ON HARDDRIVE: DEREK TAKES TRAIN RIDE
DEREK UPSOUND
“Well we did want to pay but as you can see…”

VO
It’s not clear whether it’s from commuters that PRASA expects to turn a profit. But newly appointed CEO Zolani Kgosi Matthews – the first permanent CEO in five years – is expected to turn the tide. While he finds his feet, Ramatlakane says PRASA will regain commuters’ trust.

FILE ON HARRDRIVE: JACO PRASA: CHAIRPERSON
8’10’03’13’
SUPER@ LEONARD RAMATHLAKANE: PRASA CHAIRMAN
“The people have lost confidence in railway transport but now we are working together with the people to bring back the rail”

VO
Working with people is part of PRASA’s newly-minted security strategy. Volunteers from communities all along PRASA lines have been selceted to assist in guarding the railways.

FILE ON HARRDRIVE: JACO PRASA: CHAIRPERSON
8’12’35’44’-8’13’04’14
SUPER@ LEONARD RAMATHLAKANE: PRASA CHAIRMAN
“they are the force multiplier the eyes and the ears of the police and Prasa as to what is happening. Because from their home they can see what is happening at the stations because they are close by.”

VO
The initiative is called the the People’s responsibility to Protect PRASA. But the security plan and how volunteers were chosen, seem short on detail. Even the volunteers themselves would not tell us anything about their new jobs.

FILE IN HARDDRIVE: PRASA WIMPERS
UPSOUND
A007C162_210315IC
12’13’35’01
DEREK: You don’t know anything about the payment or the training?
REPLY:
“It is private and confidential…” (MAYBE WE WILL HAVE TO SUBTITLE THIS AS THE SOUND IS NOT CLEAR

FILE IN HARDDRIVE: PRASA WIMPERS
DEREK LINK
A007C163_210315NZ
“Well, we have been trying to speak to the volunteers themselves about coming up against armed criminals, what training they will get, how much they will be paid… but either they have been told not to speak to us by PRASA or they actually don’t know”

VO
Reluctant to let us speak to recuits, PRASA representatives eventually briefed one of the volunteers to answer our questions.

FILE IN HARDDRIVE: PRASA WIMPERS
A007C156_210315GG
12’02’21’12’
DEREK
“How did you go about finding these volunteers?

SUPER@ BEN NGWASHENG: ATTRIDGEVILLE VOLUNTEER (MAY NEED SUBSTITLES IF SOUND IS WEIRD)
“No it is not about finding them, volunteers are volunteers, they will just come for the love of the country.”

FILE IN HARDDRIVE: PRASA WIMPERS
A007C155_21031543
11’55’36’00’
DEREK: “And what will they be paid for their duties?”

SUPER@ BEN NGWASHENG: ATTRIDGEVILLE VOLUNTEER
“It’s a stipend, but it hasn’t happened yet at this point in time. We are so glad that Prasa introduced the PR2P project and recognizing us officially so…they keep asking that. But according to our thinking it should be like something less than 3500 but I am not sure. People are not working they are just coming to this project…”

VO
Nearly ten thousand volunteers have been selected and if each is paid R3500 a month, taxpayers will foot a bill of nearly half a billion Rand a year.

SUPER@ STEVE HARRIS: UNTU: PRESIDENT
14’25”- 15’05”
“what role are they gonna. Play? the community is gonna stand there and they are gonna see something happening, what they gonna do? They are gonna pick up the phone and phone the South African police services. Is the police going to react or be quick enough to respond?

VO
Volunteers will work alongside the police, Umkhonto we Sizwe veterans, security companies
and reservists to prevent vandalism and of course, the illegal invasion of railway land.

8’8’40’22
DEREK
Minister can you really assure, with all the security plans plan is going to work? it just sounds fluffy to me”
8’8’41’01-8’8’50’38
“No, It will work. Noting is cast in stone. It will work… it is not like before”
8’09’21’17’-8’09’31’18
“Just be hopeful that you will see change and that change will be happening and is being implemented as we speak”


PROMOS

PROMO 1: On its knees since lockdown, commuter rail network PRASA first needs to restore security- now volunteers will be paid to spy on vandals and thieves. We investigate the state’s new plan.

PROMO 2: Run down and vandalised, commuter rail service PRASA is on its knees, failing the poor- how will the government be able to get the crucial service back on track?

PROMO 3: Thousands have invaded the tracks, infrastructure has been vandalised, but the state says a mulit-billion Rand turnaround plan will fix all that lock-down broke at Prasa- we investigate

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): railway transport grinding to a halt...
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Is the provision of security by MK members on Prasa railways the solution to the protection of the railways?
metadata.Summary: South Africans are not using trains anymore. The railways are destroyed. Trains on the main line in Cape Town have to stop 12km outside the city because illegal land invaders have occupied the railways and they are not going to move soon. MK veterans will now be given the power to protect, and community members will be paid to do what?
metadata.Further information: Shortly after the minister of transport, Fikile Mbalula appointed Zolani Matthews as the new CEO of PRASA, who critics say is too old and does not have the skills or experience to restore the embattled state-owned enterprise, the minister had another surprise up his sleeve. MK members will now be deployed to secure the railways. These MK members will be working with local communities living around the railway lines, who will be paid a stipend to help protect the railways. This is Mbalula’s plan to blow life back into the perished railway system. He has also suggested to the new CEO, Zolani Matthews that his immediate focus should be to curb corruption within PRASA and get rid of those who are just there to “eat”. This, while train services that are supposed to cater for the poorest of the poor, are practically non-existent. And as a result, they have learned not to depend on railway transport. The National Household transport survey was just released by STATSSA and shows a 45% decrease since 2013, in the number of people dependent on the railway system.
